confirmed: Source is the 23-page arXiv:2609.13494v1 [cs.HC] preprint dated 11 Sep 2026; title and eight authors match the form (PDF p. 1). The entire markdown and all PDF pages were read.

One field experiment randomly assigned intact, previously self-selected student teams to a GenAI-plus-XR workflow or usual coursework; field_rct, team assignment, between-group structure, and has_randomized_people_study = true are supported (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.1-3.4).

The course enrolled 35 sophomore architectural engineering students in nine teams; two teams declined before random assignment. Seven teams participated: four GenARch teams with N = 16 and three Control teams with N = 11; the abstract explicitly states 27 students (PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 6, Section 3.4).

No separate analyzed-person count is printed; null analyzed-person counts are appropriate. Seven team products were evaluated, and the participant pool is below 50, supporting core = no, criterion_2 = not_met, and context_class = none (PDF pp. 6, 11, 17, Sections 3.4, 4.2, 6.5; creativity-codebook.md, Section 3).

The creative task was a community gathering-space design addressing daylight, artificial lighting, and inspiration from nature and everyday experience. GenARch used DALL-E 3, Shap-E, TripoSR, Tripo3D, Arkio, and Meta Quest 3; Class 1 included a 15-minute tutorial and 35-minute ideation activity, and Class 2 a 10-minute tutorial and 80-minute XR activity (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 3.1-3.5).

The output was the team design presentation, evaluated with a 1-5 rubric including Design Innovation by two professors and five senior architectural engineering students. The panel was blinded to condition; the paper explicitly avoids calling it a panel of professional experts (PDF p. 8, Section 3.5 and Table 1). This supports the output-scored creativity eligibility criterion.

Overall presentation scores are exactly GenARch 3.45 [2.89, 3.92] and Control 3.87 [3.63, 3.88] out of 5, reported as median [IQR], not means or confidence intervals. The overall reported string and one-line finding reproduce these numbers correctly; nonsignificance refers to presentation comparisons (PDF p. 11, Section 4.2; p. 12, Figure 4 caption).

Design Innovation Kendall's W is 0.256 before adjustment and 0.342 after the criterion-specific leave-one-rater-out procedure. Its condition medians and IQRs appear only graphically; the paper states that GenARch medians were lower on all five presentation criteria without statistically significant between-condition differences (PDF p. 9, Section 3.6; p. 11, Section 4.2; p. 12, Figure 4a, also inspected visually).

Supplementary Appendix A is the evaluation rubric, B the interview protocol, and C additional experimental details; they are referenced but absent from this PDF and were not read. The PDF ends with references and has no embedded files (PDF pp. 8-10 and 18-23).

The treatment combines GenAI, XR, and extra tutorials within the broader course workflow; the paper does not isolate a GenAI-only effect (PDF p. 17, Section 6.5). This is one empirical study, not a synthesis, so the default null synthesis counts are appropriate (PDF pp. 5-9, Method).
summary: The PDF confirms a team-randomized study of 27 students with rated design outputs, correctly classified as field_rct with context_class none and below the 50-person threshold. The reported presentation statistics match, but unit counts, scoring details, outcome coverage, template fields, exclusion wording, and the supporting-materials URL need correction.
